newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says IMF okays lower 1997 budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Manila says IMF okays lower 1997 budget surplus.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) had agreed to a lower budget surplus of 7.1 billion pesos for this year, Central Bank officials said on Thursday.

The IMF mission initially balked at the idea of cutting the fiscal surplus target from the original 13 billion pesos, but officials said the Philippine panel was able to convince them that the delay in the passage of the crucial income tax bill would affect tax collection.
Latest data showed the budget surplus was at 4.52 billion pesos as of June 15, lower than the targetted 8.82 billion for the period.
The IMF has also approved the revised inflation target of 5.2 to 5.7 percent from the earlier 6.0 to 6.5.
The GNP and GDP growth rates have been maintained, the officials said.
The IMF mission is reviewing the latest economic performance and targets in preparation for an extension of the three-year Extended Fund Facility which was to expire last June.
The Philippines has asked for an extension so it can pass the income tax bill by October.
